types.embedding_query_text: WholesaleInflation: A general rise in the prices of goods at the wholesale level, before they reach consumers. Also called ProducerInflation, IndustrialInflation, BusinessInflation. Examples: US wholesale inflation, wholesale inflation.

chosen_type.label: WholesaleInflation
chosen_type.definition: A general rise in the prices of goods at the wholesale level, before they reach consumers.
chosen_type.justification: No schema.org class directly represents the economic phenomenon of wholesale inflation. 'Intangible' is a suitable parent for abstract concepts.

candidates.label: WholesaleStore
candidates.comment: A local business that sells goods in large quantities, typically to retailers or other businesses, rather than directly to individual consumers. Also called wholesaler, bulk store, cash and carry. Examples: Costco Business Center, a restaurant supply store, a building materials wholesaler.

candidates.label: DeliveryChargeSpecification
candidates.comment: A price specification detailing the cost associated with delivering an offer using a particular method. Also called Shipping cost, delivery fee, freight charge, postage cost. Examples: "Standard shipping: $5.99", "Express delivery: $15.00", "Free delivery for orders over $50". Distinct from DeliveryMethod, which describes the method itself, not its cost.

candidates.label: CompoundPriceSpecification
candidates.comment: A price specification that combines multiple prices applicable for different dimensions of consumption. Also called bundled price, multi-component price, composite pricing. Examples: A utility bill with separate charges for electricity and water, a rental agreement with base rent and a "final cleaning" fee, a software license with per-user and per-feature costs. Distinct from PriceSpecification, which is a general description of a price.

candidates.label: UnitPriceSpecification
candidates.comment: A structured value detailing the price asked for a specific offer by an organization or person. Also called price details, cost specification, offer price. Examples: "$10.99 per item", "€50 per hour", "£2.50 per unit".

candidates.label: ExchangeRateSpecification
candidates.comment: An ExchangeRateSpecification is a StructuredValue representing details about an exchange rate. Also called currency exchange rate, foreign exchange rate. Examples: The exchange rate between USD and EUR, a specific conversion rate for a financial transaction, details including fees and validity period.

types.embedding_query_text: Month: A calendar month, a division of the year. Also called CalendarMonth, PeriodOfMonth. Examples: July, June, May.

chosen_type.label: Month
chosen_type.definition: One of the twelve periods of time into which a year is divided.
chosen_type.justification: None of the candidates represent a calendar month. 'Duration' is the closest parent for a defined period of time.

candidates.label: Date
candidates.comment: Date is a data type representing a specific calendar date, typically formatted according to ISO 8601. Also called calendar date, specific day. Examples: "2023-10-27", "1999-12-31", "0001-01-01".

candidates.label: Schedule
candidates.comment: A definition of a repeating time period used to describe a regularly occurring event, specifying frequency, days, and start/end times. Also called timetable, recurring event plan, calendar entry, routine. Examples: a weekly yoga class schedule, a bus route timetable, a daily meeting schedule, a concert series calendar.

candidates.label: Season
candidates.comment: A distinct period within a media series, such as a television show, radio program, or video game. Also called media season, series installment, broadcast season. Examples: 'Season 1 of Game of Thrones', 'The Fall 2023 radio season', 'Chapter 3 of a video game series'. Distinct from TVSeason, which is specifically for television broadcasts.

candidates.label: DayOfWeek
candidates.comment: An enumeration representing a specific day of the week, used for scheduling or recurring events. Also called Weekday, calendar day, day name. Examples: Monday, Tuesday, Saturday, Sunday. Distinct from Date, which specifies a particular calendar date.

candidates.label: CreativeWorkSeason
candidates.comment: A CreativeWorkSeason is a distinct period or installment within a larger media series, such as a television show, radio program, or video game. Also called TV season, media season, series season, broadcast season. Examples: "Game of Thrones Season 8," "The Crown Season 4," "The Mandalorian Season 2." Distinct from CreativeWorkSeries, which is the entire collection of seasons or related works.

types.embedding_query_text: BusinessCosts: Expenses incurred by businesses in the course of their operations. Also called OperatingCosts, CompanyExpenses, EnterpriseCosts. Examples: Businesses’ costs.

chosen_type.label: BusinessCosts
chosen_type.definition: Expenses incurred by businesses in the course of their operations.
chosen_type.justification: No schema.org class directly represents general business costs. 'Intangible' is a suitable parent for abstract economic concepts.

candidates.label: BusinessFunction
candidates.comment: A BusinessFunction is an Enumeration specifying the type of activity or access rights offered by an organization through an offer. Also called commercial activity, service type, transaction type. Examples: Sell, LeaseOut, Repair, ProvideService, Buy.

candidates.label: DrugCost
candidates.comment: A DrugCost is a MedicalEntity representing the cost per unit of a medical drug, typically referring to wholesale or average retail cost, not an offer price. Also called medication price, pharmaceutical expense, drug expenditure. Examples: Average retail cost of a prescription, wholesale price of a vaccine, maximum reimbursable cost for a generic drug.

candidates.label: DrugCostCategory
candidates.comment: A DrugCostCategory is a MedicalEnumeration of predefined categories for medical drug costs. Also called medication cost type, pharmaceutical pricing category. Examples: Retail, Wholesale, Reimbursement.

candidates.label: HealthPlanCostSharingSpecification
candidates.comment: A HealthPlanCostSharingSpecification is an intangible description of the patient's financial responsibilities, such as deductibles, copayments, and coinsurance, under a specific health insurance plan. Also called patient cost details, insurance out-of-pocket, healthcare expense breakdown. Examples: a document detailing a plan's deductible, copay for specialist visits, coinsurance percentage. Distinct from HealthInsurancePlan, which is the overall policy, and HealthPlanFormulary, which focuses specifically on prescription drug costs.

candidates.label: MedicalBusiness
candidates.comment: A local business operating for medical purposes, which can be physical or virtual. Also called healthcare business, medical practice, health services provider. Examples: a dental office, a physical therapy clinic, a telemedicine service, a diagnostic lab. Distinct from LocalBusiness, which is a broader category for any local business.

types.embedding_query_text: Period: A defined length of time. Also called Timeframe, Duration, Interval. Examples: recent months, months ahead, 12 months that ended in July, near future.

chosen_type.label: Duration
chosen_type.definition: The length of time that something continues or lasts.
chosen_type.justification: 'Duration' perfectly matches the definition of 'a defined length of time' and the provided examples.

candidates.label: Duration
candidates.comment: As a Quantity, Duration represents a period of time, typically expressed in ISO 8601 format. Also called time span, period, length of time. Examples: "PT1H30M" (1 hour 30 minutes), "P3D" (3 days), "PT2H" (2 hours).

candidates.label: Schedule
candidates.comment: A definition of a repeating time period used to describe a regularly occurring event, specifying frequency, days, and start/end times. Also called timetable, recurring event plan, calendar entry, routine. Examples: a weekly yoga class schedule, a bus route timetable, a daily meeting schedule, a concert series calendar.

candidates.label: ServicePeriod
candidates.comment: A structured value representing a duration for a service, often including constraints like cutoff times or business days. Also called service duration, operational window, delivery timeframe, handling period. Examples: a 2-day shipping period with a 3 PM cutoff, a 5-business-day processing time, a 24/7 support period.

candidates.label: Time
candidates.comment: A data type representing a specific point in time, typically in hh:mm:ss format, potentially with a timezone offset. Also called timestamp, clock time, time of day. Examples: "14:30:00", "09:00:00Z", "17:45:30+01:00".

candidates.label: DateTime
candidates.comment: A data type representing a specific point in time, combining both date and time components according to ISO 8601. Also called Timestamp, date and time string, ISO 8601 datetime. Examples: "2023-10-27T10:30:00Z", "1999-12-31T23:59:59-05:00", "2024-01-15T14:00:00". Distinct from Date, which only specifies a calendar date without time.

types.embedding_query_text: Consumer: An individual who purchases goods and services for personal use. Also called Customer, Buyer, EndUser. Examples: consumers.

chosen_type.label: Audience
chosen_type.justification: 'Audience' is the best fit for a group of people (consumers) for whom goods and services are intended.

candidates.label: UserReview
candidates.comment: A review or critique created by an end-user, such as a consumer or attendee, rather than a professional critic. Also called customer review, consumer feedback, public review. Examples: a customer's product review on an e-commerce site, a diner's restaurant review, an audience member's movie review. Distinct from CriticReview, which is a review written by a professional critic.

candidates.label: Patient
candidates.comment: A Patient, as a MedicalAudience, is any person receiving health care services. Also called healthcare recipient, medical client, care receiver. Examples: a person visiting a doctor for a check-up, someone undergoing surgery, a person receiving therapy. Distinct from Physician, who provides medical care.

candidates.label: Audience
candidates.comment: An Audience is an Intangible entity representing the specific group of people for whom an item or creative work is intended. Also called target group, readership, viewership, demographic. Examples: children, teenagers, medical professionals, general public, investors.

candidates.label: Researcher
candidates.comment: A Researcher is an Audience type representing individuals engaged in scientific or academic inquiry. Also called scientist, academic, scholar. Examples: a university professor, a lab scientist, a PhD student, an independent scholar.

candidates.label: PurchaseType
candidates.comment: PurchaseType is an Enumeration listing different types of purchases for an item. Also called buying type, acquisition method. Examples: outright purchase, subscription, rental, lease.

types.embedding_query_text: EconomicIndex: A statistical measure that tracks changes in an economy or financial market. Also called MarketIndex, FinancialIndex, EconomicIndicator. Examples: The Producer Price Index, Core PPI, July Consumer Price Index, PPI.

chosen_type.label: EconomicIndex
chosen_type.definition: A statistical measure that tracks changes in an economy or financial market.
chosen_type.justification: No schema.org class directly represents a statistical economic index. 'StatisticalVariable' is a suitable parent for a measurable statistical metric.

candidates.label: ExchangeRateSpecification
candidates.comment: An ExchangeRateSpecification is a StructuredValue representing details about an exchange rate. Also called currency exchange rate, foreign exchange rate. Examples: The exchange rate between USD and EUR, a specific conversion rate for a financial transaction, details including fees and validity period.

candidates.label: FinancialIncentive
candidates.comment: A FinancialIncentive is an Intangible representing financial benefits offered for goods or services, including details like amount, status, and eligibility criteria. Also called rebate, subsidy, grant, discount. Examples: A government tax credit for electric vehicles, a manufacturer's rebate on an appliance, a low-interest loan program, a student scholarship.

candidates.label: MedicalRiskScore
candidates.comment: A medical risk estimator that is a simple system summing risk factors to yield a score associated with prognosis. Also called clinical score, prognostic score, risk index. Examples: "CHAD score", "TIMI risk score", "APACHE II score". Distinct from MedicalRiskCalculator, which involves more complex mathematical calculations.

candidates.label: CompoundPriceSpecification
candidates.comment: A price specification that combines multiple prices applicable for different dimensions of consumption. Also called bundled price, multi-component price, composite pricing. Examples: A utility bill with separate charges for electricity and water, a rental agreement with base rent and a "final cleaning" fee, a software license with per-user and per-feature costs. Distinct from PriceSpecification, which is a general description of a price.

candidates.label: PriceSpecification
candidates.comment: A PriceSpecification is a StructuredValue representing a price or price range, typically used for markup of offers. Also called pricing details, cost specification. Examples: a product's list price, a service's hourly rate, a discount price, a price range for a flight. Distinct from MonetaryAmount, which describes independent amounts of money.

types.embedding_query_text: EconomicActorGroup: A collective of entities involved in economic activities, such as production or manufacturing. Also called IndustryGroup, BusinessGroup, EconomicSector. Examples: producers and manufacturers, manufacturers.

chosen_type.label: EconomicActorGroup
chosen_type.definition: A collective of entities involved in economic activities, such as production or manufacturing.
chosen_type.justification: None of the candidates precisely describe a group of economic actors by their role. 'Organization' is a suitable parent for a group of entities.

candidates.label: Consortium
candidates.comment: A membership organization typically composed of other organizations collaborating on a shared project or goal. Also called alliance, syndicate, federation, partnership. Examples: World Wide Web Consortium (W3C), a research consortium, a banking consortium, a joint venture. Distinct from Organization, which is a general grouping of people or entities.

candidates.label: PerformingGroup
candidates.comment: A PerformingGroup is an organization of performers, such as a band, orchestra, or circus. Also called performance ensemble, troupe, artistic group. Examples: Cirque du Soleil, a local theatre company, a dance troupe. Distinct from MusicGroup, which is specifically for musical performers.

candidates.label: MusicGroup
candidates.comment: A MusicGroup, as a PerformingGroup, is an organization of musicians, such as a band or orchestra, or a solo musician. Also called band, musical ensemble, orchestra, solo artist. Examples: The Beatles, New York Philharmonic, Taylor Swift. Distinct from PerformingGroup, which is a broader category for any performance group.

candidates.label: Cooperative
candidates.comment: A Cooperative is an organization formed as a joint project by multiple organizations or individuals, often for mutual benefit. Also called member-owned business, co-op, collective. Examples: REI (Recreational Equipment, Inc.), Ocean Spray, Sunkist Growers, credit unions. Distinct from Corporation, which is a business entity owned by shareholders.

candidates.label: TheaterGroup
candidates.comment: An organization or company dedicated to producing and performing theatrical works. Also called theater company, drama troupe, acting ensemble. Examples: The Royal Shakespeare Company, Cirque du Soleil, a local amateur dramatics society.

types.embedding_query_text: Percentage: A rate, number, or amount in each hundred. Also called Rate, Proportion, Ratio. Examples: 4.7%, 5.5%, 0.1%, 5.9%.

chosen_type.label: Number
chosen_type.justification: A percentage is a numerical value, making 'Number' the most appropriate data type.

candidates.label: ExchangeRateSpecification
candidates.comment: An ExchangeRateSpecification is a StructuredValue representing details about an exchange rate. Also called currency exchange rate, foreign exchange rate. Examples: The exchange rate between USD and EUR, a specific conversion rate for a financial transaction, details including fees and validity period.

candidates.label: MonetaryAmount
candidates.comment: A structured value representing a monetary value or range, typically expressed with a currency. Also called amount of money, financial value, currency amount. Examples: "$50 USD", "£1,000 to £1,000,000 GBP", "€25.99". Distinct from PriceSpecification, which describes the price of an offer.

candidates.label: TierBenefitEnumeration
candidates.comment: An enumeration of specific benefits offered as part of a loyalty or membership program. Also called loyalty program benefit, membership perk, reward tier. Examples: free shipping, early access to sales, exclusive content, dedicated customer support.

candidates.label: Number
candidates.comment: Number is a data type representing numerical values. Also called numeric value, quantity, digit. Examples: 10, 3.14, -5, 1000000. Distinct from Text, which represents character strings.

candidates.label: HyperTocEntry
candidates.comment: A HyperTocEntry is a creative work representing an individual item or section within a HyperToc, specifying its associated media and time offsets. Also called table of contents item, media chapter, section marker. Examples: 'Introduction (0:00-5:30)', 'Keynote Speech (10:15-30:00)', 'Q&A Session (30:00-45:00)'.

types.embedding_query_text: GovernmentAgency: A permanent or semi-permanent organization in the machinery of government responsible for the oversight and administration of specific functions. Also called PublicAgency, StateDepartment, GovernmentBody. Examples: Bureau of Labor Statistics, Bureau of Labor Statistics data.

chosen_type.label: GovernmentOrganization
chosen_type.justification: 'GovernmentOrganization' is a perfect fit for an organization that is part of a governmental body, such as the Bureau of Labor Statistics.

candidates.label: GovernmentOrganization
candidates.comment: A GovernmentOrganization is an organization or agency that is part of a governmental body. Also called public sector entity, state agency, governmental body. Examples: Department of Defense, Environmental Protection Agency, National Institutes of Health, local city council.

candidates.label: EmploymentAgency
candidates.comment: An EmploymentAgency is a LocalBusiness that helps individuals find jobs and employers find suitable candidates. Also called recruitment agency, staffing firm, job placement service. Examples: A temporary staffing agency, an executive search firm, a headhunting company.

candidates.label: GovernmentPermit
candidates.comment: A GovernmentPermit is a formal authorization issued by a government agency. Also called public license, state approval, official authorization. Examples: building permit, driver's license, business operating license, fishing permit.

candidates.label: GovernmentOffice
candidates.comment: A GovernmentOffice is a local business representing a specific governmental agency or department. Also called public agency office, state department branch, municipal service center. Examples: IRS office, DMV office, local planning department, social security office. Distinct from GovernmentBuilding, which is the physical structure that may contain multiple offices.

candidates.label: GovernmentService
candidates.comment: A GovernmentService is an intangible service provided by a government organization to the public. Also called public service, state-provided service, municipal offering. Examples: food stamps program, veterans benefits, public education, waste collection.

types.embedding_query_text: DayOfWeek: A specific day within a calendar week. Also called Weekday, WeekendDay. Examples: Thursday, Wednesday.

chosen_type.label: DayOfWeek
chosen_type.justification: 'DayOfWeek' is a perfect fit for a specific day within a calendar week.

candidates.label: DayOfWeek
candidates.comment: An enumeration representing a specific day of the week, used for scheduling or recurring events. Also called Weekday, calendar day, day name. Examples: Monday, Tuesday, Saturday, Sunday. Distinct from Date, which specifies a particular calendar date.

candidates.comment: A definition of a repeating time period used to describe a regularly occurring event, specifying frequency, days, and start/end times. candidates.label: CreativeWorkSeason
candidates.comment: A CreativeWorkSeason is a distinct period or installment within a larger media series, such as a television show, radio program, or video game. Distinct from CreativeWorkSeries, which is the entire collection of seasons or related works.

candidates.label: Time
candidates.comment: A data type representing a specific point in time, typically in hh:mm:ss format, potentially with a timezone offset. Also called timestamp, clock time, time of day. Examples: "14:30:00", "09:00:00Z", "17:45:30+01:00".

types.embedding_query_text: Periodicity: The quality or characteristic of recurring at regular intervals. Also called Frequency, Regularity, Cycle. Examples: monthly basis.

chosen_type.label: Schedule
chosen_type.justification: 'Schedule' defines repeating time periods and frequency, which aligns well with the concept of periodicity.

candidates.label: Schedule
candidates.comment: A definition of a repeating time period used to describe a regularly occurring event, specifying frequency, days, and start/end times. Also called timetable, recurring event plan, calendar entry, routine. Examples: a weekly yoga class schedule, a bus route timetable, a daily meeting schedule, a concert series calendar.

candidates.label: Periodical
candidates.comment: A Periodical, as a CreativeWorkSeries, is a publication issued in successive parts with numerical or chronological designations, intended to continue indefinitely. Also called serial publication, magazine, journal. Examples: The New Yorker magazine, a scholarly journal, a daily newspaper. Distinct from Book, which is a single, non-serial publication.

candidates.label: Duration
candidates.comment: As a Quantity, Duration represents a period of time, typically expressed in ISO 8601 format. Also called time span, period, length of time. Examples: "PT1H30M" (1 hour 30 minutes), "P3D" (3 days), "PT2H" (2 hours).

candidates.label: InstantaneousEvent
candidates.comment: An InstantaneousEvent is a structured value representing an event with no duration, such as a single point in time. Also called momentary event, point event, discrete occurrence. Examples: a computer log entry, a timestamp, a single click on a webpage. Distinct from Event, which typically has a duration.

candidates.label: EventSeries
candidates.comment: An EventSeries is an Event representing a collection of events that share unifying characteristics, such as a recurring festival or a thematic lecture series. Also called event cycle, recurring event, series of events. Examples: The Olympic Games, a monthly book club meeting, a season of a concert series, a weekly farmers market.

types.embedding_query_text: ProfessionGroup: A group of individuals sharing a common occupation or field of expertise. Also called OccupationalGroup, ProfessionalBody, SpecialistGroup. Examples: economists.

chosen_type.label: ProfessionGroup
chosen_type.definition: A collection of individuals sharing a common occupation or area of expertise.
chosen_type.justification: None of the candidates represent a group of people defined by their profession. 'Audience' is a suitable parent for a demographic group.

candidates.label: Occupation
candidates.comment: An Occupation is a profession that may involve prolonged training and/or a formal qualification. Also called profession, job, career. Examples: doctor, engineer, teacher, artist. Distinct from Role, which describes a specific function within an organization or context.

candidates.label: ProfessionalService
candidates.comment: ProfessionalService is a LocalBusiness type for providers of specialized services. Also called expert service, specialized service. Examples: a legal service, an accounting service, a dental practice, an architectural firm. Distinct from Service, which is a broader concept of an intangible offering.

candidates.label: TheaterGroup
candidates.comment: An organization or company dedicated to producing and performing theatrical works. Also called theater company, drama troupe, acting ensemble. Examples: The Royal Shakespeare Company, Cirque du Soleil, a local amateur dramatics society.

candidates.label: MusicGroup
candidates.comment: A MusicGroup, as a PerformingGroup, is an organization of musicians, such as a band or orchestra, or a solo musician. Also called band, musical ensemble, orchestra, solo artist. types.embedding_query_text: SupplyChain: The network of all the individuals, organizations, resources, activities, and technology involved in the creation and sale of a product. Also called LogisticsNetwork, DistributionChain, ProductionChain. Examples: supply chain.

chosen_type.label: SupplyChain
chosen_type.definition: The network of all individuals, organizations, resources, activities, and technology involved in the creation and sale of a product.
chosen_type.justification: No schema.org class directly represents a supply chain as a network. 'Intangible' is a suitable parent for an abstract concept or system.

candidates.label: Consortium
candidates.comment: A membership organization typically composed of other organizations collaborating on a shared project or goal. Also called alliance, syndicate, federation, partnership. Examples: World Wide Web Consortium (W3C), a research consortium, a banking consortium, a joint venture. Distinct from Organization, which is a general grouping of people or entities.

candidates.label: DeliveryEvent
candidates.comment: An event representing the delivery of an item, typically a product or package. Also called Shipping event, package delivery, consignment event. Examples: A package arriving at its destination, a food delivery being completed, a furniture delivery appointment. Distinct from Order, which is the request for items, not the delivery itself.

candidates.label: SomeProducts
candidates.comment: A placeholder representing multiple similar products of the same kind, used when specific individual products are not distinguished. Also called product group, product category, generic products, similar items. Examples: 'a batch of apples', 'several identical t-shirts', 'a collection of standard screws'.

candidates.label: MerchantReturnPolicy
candidates.comment: An intangible providing information about product return policies associated with an organization, product, or offer. Also called return policy, refund policy, merchandise return terms. Examples: "30-day return policy", "final sale policy", "return policy for electronics".

candidates.label: Project
candidates.comment: A Project is an Organization representing an enterprise, typically collaborative, planned to achieve a particular aim. Also called initiative, endeavor, venture. Examples: a software development project, a construction project, a research initiative, a community outreach program.

types.embedding_query_text: Conflict: A state of disagreement or argument between opposing forces, often involving armed struggle. Also called War, Dispute, Hostilities. Examples: war in Iran, Iran conflict, ongoing Iran conflict.

chosen_type.label: Conflict
chosen_type.definition: A serious disagreement or argument, often protracted, between parties.
chosen_type.justification: None of the candidates represent a state of conflict or war. 'Event' is a suitable parent for a significant occurrence.

candidates.label: DisagreeAction
candidates.comment: A react action expressing a negative opinion or difference of opinion regarding an object, proposition, or theme. Also called Express disagreement, object to, dispute, dissent. Examples: Disagreeing with a political statement, objecting to a proposed plan, disputing a fact. Distinct from AgreeAction, which expresses positive sentiment or agreement.

candidates.label: Conversation
candidates.comment: A series of one or more messages exchanged between individuals or organizations on a specific topic. Also called discussion, dialogue, chat, discourse. Examples: An email thread, a text message exchange, a forum discussion, a spoken dialogue. Distinct from Comment, which is a single remark on an item.

candidates.label: PoliticalParty
candidates.comment: A PoliticalParty is an Organization formed to contest elections and hold power in government. Also called political movement, party. Examples: Democratic Party, Republican Party, Labour Party, Conservative Party.

candidates.label: Claim
candidates.comment: A specific, factually-oriented statement that can be reviewed for accuracy. Also called assertion, statement, proposition, contention. Examples: "The Earth is flat," "Coffee cures cancer," "This product is 100% organic." Distinct from ClaimReview, which is the review of a claim.

candidates.label: State
candidates.comment: A major administrative division of a country, such as a state or province. Also called province, region, territory, commonwealth. Examples: California, Ontario, Bavaria, Texas.

types.embedding_query_text: CommodityPrice: The market value of a raw material or primary agricultural product. Also called RawMaterialCost, ResourcePrice, GoodsPrice. Examples: oil and gas prices, fuel prices, energy prices.

chosen_type.label: PriceSpecification

candidates.label: ExchangeRateSpecification

types.embedding_query_text: Commodity: A raw material or primary agricultural product that can be bought and sold. Also called RawMaterial, Product, Good. Examples: other commodities.

chosen_type.label: Product
chosen_type.justification: A commodity is a type of 'Product' that can be bought and sold.

candidates.label: Product
candidates.comment: A Product is any offered good or service. Also called item, merchandise, offering. Examples: a pair of shoes, a concert ticket, a car rental service, an episode of a TV show.

candidates.label: SomeProducts
candidates.comment: A placeholder representing multiple similar products of the same kind, used when specific individual products are not distinguished. Also called product group, product category, generic products, similar items. Examples: 'a batch of apples', 'several identical t-shirts', 'a collection of standard screws'.

candidates.label: DietarySupplement
candidates.comment: A product taken orally that contains dietary ingredients intended to supplement the diet, such as vitamins, minerals, or herbs. Also called Nutritional supplement, health supplement, vitamin, herbal remedy. Examples: Multivitamin pills, fish oil capsules, protein powder, ginseng extract. Distinct from Drug, which is primarily for treating, preventing, or diagnosing disease.

candidates.label: Vehicle
candidates.comment: A device designed or used for transporting people or cargo across various environments. Also called conveyance, transport, automobile. Examples: a car, a bicycle, an airplane, a boat, a truck.

candidates.label: IndividualProduct
candidates.comment: An IndividualProduct is a single, identifiable instance of a product. Also called specific product unit, unique item, serialized product. Examples: a laptop with a specific serial number, a particular copy of a book, a unique piece of art. Distinct from ProductModel, which describes a class of products, and ProductGroup, which is a collection of products.

types.embedding_query_text: ProducerInflation: Inflation measured at the producer or wholesale level, reflecting changes in the prices received by domestic producers for their output. Also called WholesalePriceInflation, FactoryGateInflation, InputCostInflation. Examples: Producer-level inflation.

chosen_type.label: ProducerInflation
chosen_type.definition: Inflation measured at the producer or wholesale level, reflecting changes in the prices received by domestic producers for their output.

candidates.label: CompoundPriceSpecification

candidates.label: ExchangeRateSpecification

candidates.label: UnitPriceSpecification
candidates.comment: A structured value detailing the price asked for a specific offer by an organization or person. Also called price details, cost specification, offer price. Examples: "$10.99 per item", "€50 per hour", "£2.50 per unit".

candidates.label: DeliveryChargeSpecification

candidates.label: PriceSpecification
candidates.comment: A PriceSpecification is a StructuredValue representing a price or price range, typically used for markup of offers. Also called pricing details, cost specification. Examples: a product's list price, a service's hourly rate, a discount price, a price range for a flight. Distinct from MonetaryAmount, which describes independent amounts of money.

types.embedding_query_text: MetricLevel: A specific point or degree on a scale of measurement. Also called Level, Degree, Threshold. Examples: four-year high, lowest rate.

chosen_type.label: Rating

candidates.label: MedicalEvidenceLevel

candidates.label: LegalValueLevel

candidates.label: MonetaryAmount

candidates.label: Rating

candidates.label: MeasurementMethodEnum
candidates.comment: An enumeration of methods used for measurement. Also called measurement technique, gauging method, assessment approach. Examples: "manual measurement", "automated sensor measurement", "self-reported measurement".

candidates.label: GroceryStore

candidates.label: DrugCost

candidates.label: FoodService

chosen_type.justification: None of the candidates represent the abstract concept of household finances. 'Intangible' is a suitable parent for such a domain.

candidates.label: SingleFamilyResidence
candidates.comment: A type of house designed to be occupied by one family, typically detached from other homes. Also called detached house, single-family home, private residence. Examples: a suburban house with a yard, a standalone cottage, a bungalow.

candidates.label: FinancialService
candidates.comment: A FinancialService is a LocalBusiness that provides financial services. Also called bank, credit union, investment firm, insurance company. Examples: A retail bank, a wealth management firm, an insurance agency, a loan provider.

candidates.label: FinancialIncentive
candidates.comment: A FinancialIncentive is an Intangible representing financial benefits offered for goods or services, including details like amount, status, and eligibility criteria. Also called rebate, subsidy, grant, discount. Examples: A government tax credit for electric vehicles, a manufacturer's rebate on an appliance, a low-interest loan program, a student scholarship.

candidates.label: BankOrCreditUnion
candidates.comment: A FinancialService provided by an institution that handles money and credit for customers. Also called bank, credit union, financial institution. Examples: "Chase Bank", "Navy Federal Credit Union", "Citibank". Distinct from AutomatedTeller, which is a machine, not an institution.

types.embedding_query_text: EconomicConcept: An abstract idea or general notion relating to economics. Also called EconomicPrinciple, MarketIdea, FinancialConcept. Examples: affordability.

Also called rebate, subsidy, grant, discount. Examples: A government tax credit for electric vehicles, a manufacturer's rebate on an appliance, a low-interest loan program, a student scholarship.

candidates.label: FinancialProduct
candidates.comment: A FinancialProduct is a Service provided by financial institutions to consumers and businesses. Also called financial instrument, banking product, investment product. Examples: A savings account, a mortgage loan, an insurance policy, a mutual fund.

candidates.label: BankAccount
candidates.comment: A FinancialProduct or service offered by a bank for depositing, withdrawing, or transferring money, often with interest. Also called bank account, checking account, savings account, deposit account. Examples: "My personal checking account", "A business savings account", "A joint current account".

candidates.label: LoanOrCredit
candidates.comment: A financial product representing an amount of money loaned or a line of credit offered under specific terms and charges. Also called credit facility, lending product, financial loan. Examples: a personal loan, a credit card, a mortgage, a business line of credit. Distinct from MortgageLoan, which is specifically a loan secured by real estate.

candidates.label: HealthPlanCostSharingSpecification
candidates.comment: A HealthPlanCostSharingSpecification is an intangible description of the patient's financial responsibilities, such as deductibles, copayments, and coinsurance, under a specific health insurance plan. Also called patient cost details, insurance out-of-pocket, healthcare expense breakdown. Examples: a document detailing a plan's deductible, copay for specialist visits, coinsurance percentage. Distinct from HealthInsurancePlan, which is the overall policy, and HealthPlanFormulary, which focuses specifically on prescription drug costs.

types.embedding_query_text: Report: A factual account or statement about a particular subject. Also called Document, Statement, Publication. Examples: latest PPI report, Thursday’s report.

chosen_type.label: Report
chosen_type.justification: 'Report' is a perfect fit for a factual account or statement, such as a 'PPI report'.

candidates.label: Report
candidates.comment: A Report is an Article generated by a governmental or non-governmental organization. Also called official report, document, publication. Examples: an annual financial report, a government research report, a UN policy report, a company's sustainability report.

candidates.label: ReportageNewsArticle
candidates.comment: A ReportageNewsArticle is a NewsArticle representing news articles based on factual journalistic reporting, emphasizing verified information and multiple viewpoints. Also called news report, journalistic article, factual news. Examples: a breaking news story about a political event, an investigative report on a social issue, a factual account of a natural disaster, a report on scientific findings. Distinct from AnalysisNewsArticle, which goes deeper into analysis.

candidates.label: Statement
candidates.comment: A declaration or assertion about something, often a fact or an interesting piece of information. Also called assertion, declaration, factoid, claim. Examples: 'The Earth is round', 'Water boils at 100 degrees Celsius', 'The capital of France is Paris'. Distinct from Claim, which is used for more formal, verifiable assertions in fact-checking.

candidates.label: Article
candidates.comment: An Article is a CreativeWork, typically a written piece such as a news report, magazine feature, or investigative report. Also called written piece, report, feature, essay, column. Examples: a newspaper article about local politics, a magazine feature on travel, a scientific journal article, a blog post. Distinct from BlogPosting, which is a specific type of article published on a blog.

candidates.label: AnalysisNewsArticle
candidates.comment: An AnalysisNewsArticle is a NewsArticle that combines factual reporting with the author's expertise, offering interpretations and conclusions. Also called news analysis, interpretive news, expert commentary. Examples: An article analyzing the economic impact of a new policy, a piece interpreting election results, a report on scientific findings with expert commentary. Distinct from NewsArticle, which primarily focuses on factual reporting without extensive interpretation.

types.embedding_query_text: Season: One of the four divisions of the year based on changes in weather, ecology, and hours of daylight. Also called TimeOfYear, PeriodOfYear. Examples: summer.

chosen_type.label: CalendarSeason
chosen_type.definition: A period of the year characterized by particular weather conditions, or a specific period in sports or entertainment.
chosen_type.justification: The schema.org 'Season' is specific to media series. 'CalendarSeason' is a new type for natural seasons, with 'Duration' as a suitable parent.

candidates.label: Season
candidates.comment: A distinct period within a media series, such as a television show, radio program, or video game. Also called media season, series installment, broadcast season. Examples: 'Season 1 of Game of Thrones', 'The Fall 2023 radio season', 'Chapter 3 of a video game series'. Distinct from TVSeason, which is specifically for television broadcasts.

candidates.label: CreativeWorkSeason
candidates.comment: A CreativeWorkSeason is a distinct period or installment within a larger media series, such as a television show, radio program, or video game. Also called TV season, media season, series season, broadcast season. Examples: "Game of Thrones Season 8," "The Crown Season 4," "The Mandalorian Season 2." Distinct from CreativeWorkSeries, which is the entire collection of seasons or related works.

candidates.label: TVSeason
candidates.comment: A distinct period of a television series, comprising multiple episodes, dedicated to TV broadcast and associated online delivery. Also called television season, broadcast season, show season. Examples: 'Season 1 of The Crown', 'The final season of Breaking Bad'. Distinct from Season, which is a more general media season.

candidates.label: Schedule
candidates.comment: A definition of a repeating time period used to describe a regularly occurring event, specifying frequency, days, and start/end times. Also called timetable, recurring event plan, calendar entry, routine. Examples: a weekly yoga class schedule, a bus route timetable, a daily meeting schedule, a concert series calendar.

candidates.label: PodcastSeason
candidates.comment: A PodcastSeason is a CreativeWorkSeason representing a single season of a podcast, used when a podcast is structured into distinct seasons. Also called podcast series season. Examples: "Serial" Season 1, "Lore" Season 3, a specific season of a narrative podcast. Distinct from PodcastSeries, which is the entire podcast collection.

types.embedding_query_text: Person: An individual human being. Also called Individual, Human, Agent. Examples: Ben Ayers.

chosen_type.label: Person
chosen_type.justification: 'Person' is a perfect fit for an individual human being.

candidates.label: Person
candidates.comment: A Person is an individual human being, whether alive, dead, undead, or fictional. Also called individual, human, character. Examples: John Doe, Albert Einstein, Sherlock Holmes. Distinct from Organization, which is a group of people.

candidates.label: IndividualPhysician
candidates.comment: An IndividualPhysician is a medical business representing a single medical practitioner. Also called doctor, medical doctor, general practitioner, specialist. Examples: Dr. Jane Smith (a family doctor), Dr. John Doe (a cardiologist), a local pediatrician. Distinct from Physician, which is the general role, and MedicalOrganization, which is a facility.

candidates.label: IndividualProduct
candidates.comment: An IndividualProduct is a single, identifiable instance of a product. Also called specific product unit, unique item, serialized product. Examples: a laptop with a specific serial number, a particular copy of a book, a unique piece of art. Distinct from ProductModel, which describes a class of products, and ProductGroup, which is a collection of products.

candidates.label: Residence
candidates.comment: A Residence is a Place where a person lives. Also called home, dwelling, abode. Examples: a house, an apartment, a condominium, a dormitory room.

candidates.label: Audience
candidates.comment: An Audience is an Intangible entity representing the specific group of people for whom an item or creative work is intended. Also called target group, readership, viewership, demographic. Examples: children, teenagers, medical professionals, general public, investors.

types.embedding_query_text: Occupation: A job or profession. Also called Profession, Job, Vocation. Examples: senior economist.

chosen_type.label: Occupation
chosen_type.justification: 'Occupation' is a perfect fit for a job or profession, such as 'senior economist'.

candidates.label: Occupation
candidates.comment: An Occupation is a profession that may involve prolonged training and/or a formal qualification. Also called profession, job, career. Examples: doctor, engineer, teacher, artist. Distinct from Role, which describes a specific function within an organization or context.

candidates.label: ProfessionalService
candidates.comment: ProfessionalService is a LocalBusiness type for providers of specialized services. Also called expert service, specialized service. Examples: a legal service, an accounting service, a dental practice, an architectural firm. Distinct from Service, which is a broader concept of an intangible offering.

candidates.label: Attorney
candidates.comment: An Attorney is a LegalService professional who practices law, providing legal advice and representation. Also called lawyer, legal counsel, barrister, solicitor. Examples: a criminal defense attorney, a corporate lawyer, a family law solicitor, a public defender. Distinct from LegalService, which is the broader category of services provided by legal professionals.

candidates.label: Specialty
candidates.comment: Any branch of a field in which individuals develop specific expertise, typically through significant study and effort. Also called area of expertise, specialization, discipline, field. Examples: 'Cardiology' as a medical specialty, 'Corporate Law' as a legal specialty, 'Artificial Intelligence' as a computer science specialty.

candidates.label: JobPosting
candidates.comment: A JobPosting is an intangible listing that describes an open position within an organization. Also called job advertisement, employment listing, career opening. Examples: a software engineer job posting, a marketing manager vacancy, a retail associate opening.

types.embedding_query_text: Organization: A structured group of people with a particular purpose. Also called Company, Institution, Association. Examples: Nationwide.

chosen_type.label: Organization
chosen_type.justification: 'Organization' is a perfect fit for a structured group of people with a particular purpose, such as 'Nationwide'.

candidates.label: Organization
candidates.comment: An Organization is a group of people with a particular purpose, such as a school, NGO, corporation, or club. Also called entity, institution, association. Examples: Google, Harvard University, Red Cross, a local sports club. Distinct from Person, which is an individual.

candidates.label: SportsOrganization
candidates.comment: A general category for organizations involved in sports, including teams, governing bodies, and associations. Also called athletic organization, sports body, sports group. Examples: the NBA, a local youth soccer league, the International Olympic Committee.

candidates.label: LocalBusiness
candidates.comment: A specific physical business or a branch of an organization that serves a local community. Also called local company, neighborhood business, regional enterprise. Examples: a local restaurant, a bank branch, a medical clinic, a bowling alley, a grocery store. Distinct from Organization, which is a broader category for any group of people with a particular purpose.

candidates.label: SearchRescueOrganization
candidates.comment: An organization dedicated to finding and providing aid to people who are lost or in imminent danger. Also called SAR team, rescue service, emergency search unit. Examples: a mountain rescue team, a coast guard search and rescue unit, a volunteer SAR group.

candidates.label: MedicalOrganization
candidates.comment: An organization, physical or virtual, operating in the medical domain, such as a hospital or clinic. Also called healthcare organization, medical institution, health system. Examples: "Mayo Clinic", "World Health Organization", "Doctors Without Borders". Distinct from Organization, which is a broader category for any group.

types.embedding_query_text: EconomicActivity: The production, distribution, and consumption of goods and services. Also called BusinessActivity, MarketActivity, CommercialActivity. Examples: massive AI build-out and investment.

chosen_type.label: TradeAction
chosen_type.justification: 'TradeAction' encompasses the exchange of goods/services and monetary compensation, which aligns with 'AI build-out and investment' as economic activities.

candidates.label: TradeAction
candidates.comment: The act of exchanging goods or services for monetary compensation. Also called commerce, transaction, selling. Examples: a business selling products to customers, a consultant providing services for a fee, an artist selling their artwork.

candidates.label: ConsumeAction
candidates.comment: The act of ingesting or utilizing information, resources, or food. Also called consumption, utilizing, ingesting, using. Examples: Reading a book, eating a meal, watching a movie, using electricity. Distinct from Action, which is a general activity.

candidates.label: SellAction
candidates.comment: The act of an agent exchanging goods or services for money with a buyer. Also called selling, vending, trading, transacting. Examples: a store selling a product to a customer, a person selling a used car, a company selling software licenses. Distinct from BuyAction, which is the reciprocal act from the buyer's perspective.

candidates.label: UseAction
candidates.comment: The act of applying an object to its intended purpose or function. Also called utilize, employ, operate. Examples: using a tool to fix something, consuming food, wearing clothes.

candidates.label: BuyAction
candidates.comment: A BuyAction is a TradeAction representing the act of an agent acquiring goods or services from a seller in exchange for money. Also called purchase action, acquire action, procure action. Examples: buying groceries, purchasing a movie ticket, subscribing to a service. Distinct from SellAction, which is the act of giving goods or services for money.

types.embedding_query_text: MonetaryValue: The worth or price of something expressed in terms of money. Also called FinancialValue, CashValue, CurrencyAmount. Examples: trillions of dollars.

chosen_type.label: MonetaryAmount
chosen_type.justification: 'MonetaryAmount' is a perfect fit for a value expressed in terms of money, such as 'trillions of dollars'.

candidates.label: MonetaryAmount
candidates.comment: A structured value representing a monetary value or range, typically expressed with a currency. Also called amount of money, financial value, currency amount. Examples: "$50 USD", "£1,000 to £1,000,000 GBP", "€25.99". Distinct from PriceSpecification, which describes the price of an offer.

candidates.label: DatedMoneySpecification
candidates.comment: A structured value representing a monetary amount that is valid or applicable over a specified time period, though its use is superseded by MonetaryAmount. Also called Time-bound monetary value, period-specific money, dated financial amount. Examples: An employee's salary from 2022-01-01 to 2022-12-31, a subscription fee valid for a quarter, a bonus paid for a specific fiscal year.

candidates.label: MonetaryAmountDistribution
candidates.comment: A quantitative value distribution representing a statistical distribution of monetary amounts. Also called money distribution, financial range, income distribution. Examples: "average salary range", "distribution of asset values", "price range for a product category".

candidates.label: QuantitativeValue
candidates.comment: A QuantitativeValue is a StructuredValue representing a point value or interval for product characteristics or other purposes. Also called numerical value, measurable value. Examples: a product's weight of '5 kg', a temperature range of '20-25°C', a height of '1.8 meters', a price of '$99.99'. Distinct from QualitativeValue, which represents a predefined, non-numeric value.

candidates.label: MonetaryGrant
candidates.comment: An intangible grant that provides a sum of money. Also called financial grant, money award, cash donation. Examples: a research grant, a scholarship, a government subsidy. Distinct from Grant, which can be non-monetary.

types.embedding_query_text: ProductCategory: A classification of goods or services based on shared characteristics. Also called GoodsCategory, ServiceCategory, ProductLine. Examples: AI-related components.

chosen_type.label: ProductGroup
chosen_type.justification: 'ProductGroup' represents a group of products with shared characteristics, which fits 'AI-related components' as a classification.

candidates.label: ProductGroup
candidates.comment: A ProductGroup is a Product representing a group of products that vary only in specific attributes like size, color, or material, serving as a template for its variants. Also called product family, product line, variant group. Examples: a specific model of smartphone available in different colors and storage sizes, a t-shirt design available in various sizes and fabrics, a car model with different trim levels. Distinct from Product, which is a specific variant offered for sale.

candidates.label: CategoryCode
candidates.comment: A defined term representing a specific code within a classification system. Also called classification code, item code, type code. Examples: UNSPSC code for office supplies, NAICS code for manufacturing, a product category ID.

candidates.label: SomeProducts
candidates.comment: A placeholder representing multiple similar products of the same kind, used when specific individual products are not distinguished. Also called product group, product category, generic products, similar items. Examples: 'a batch of apples', 'several identical t-shirts', 'a collection of standard screws'.

candidates.label: ProductCollection
candidates.comment: A ProductCollection is a Collection of products, either ProductGroups or specific variants, listed together, often within an Offer. Also called product assortment, product bundle, product set. Examples: a collection of books by an author, a bundle of software products, a set of kitchen utensils, a curated selection of wines.

candidates.label: ProductModel
candidates.comment: A ProductModel is a Product representing a datasheet or vendor specification of a prototypical product description. Also called product prototype, product specification, product blueprint. Examples: the technical specifications for a new laptop model, a design document for a car engine, a vendor's product data sheet, a conceptual product design.

types.embedding_query_text: BusinessSector: A segment of the economy that comprises businesses with similar activities or products. Also called IndustrySector, MarketSegment, EconomicSector. Examples: storage and memory suppliers.

chosen_type.label: BusinessSector
chosen_type.definition: A segment of the economy that comprises businesses with similar activities or products.
chosen_type.justification: None of the candidates represent a business sector. 'Intangible' is a suitable parent for an abstract classification.

candidates.label: BusinessFunction
candidates.comment: A BusinessFunction is an Enumeration specifying the type of activity or access rights offered by an organization through an offer. Also called commercial activity, service type, transaction type. Examples: Sell, LeaseOut, Repair, ProvideService, Buy.

candidates.label: BusinessEntityType
candidates.comment: A BusinessEntityType is an Enumeration representing the legal form, size, main line of business, or position in the value chain of an organization or business person. Also called legal entity type, company structure, business classification. Examples: Corporation, Sole Proprietorship, Partnership, Non-profit Organization.

candidates.label: SportsActivityLocation
candidates.comment: A local business or facility providing a venue for sports activities. Also called sports venue, athletic facility, recreation center, playing field. Examples: a local gym, a public tennis court, a community swimming pool, a golf course.

candidates.label: SomeProducts
candidates.comment: A placeholder representing multiple similar products of the same kind, used when specific individual products are not distinguished. Also called product group, product category, generic products, similar items. Examples: 'a batch of apples', 'several identical t-shirts', 'a collection of standard screws'.

candidates.label: BusinessEvent
candidates.comment: A BusinessEvent is an Event related to commercial activities, such as conferences, trade shows, or corporate meetings. Also called corporate event, professional gathering, industry event. Examples: a sales conference, a product launch event, an annual shareholder meeting. Distinct from SocialEvent, which is for personal or recreational gatherings.

types.embedding_query_text: Product: An article or substance that is manufactured or refined for sale. Also called Good, Merchandise, Item. Examples: high-performance memory chips, consumer products.

chosen_type.label: Product
chosen_type.justification: 'Product' is a perfect fit for an article or substance manufactured for sale, such as 'memory chips' or 'consumer products'.

candidates.label: Product
candidates.comment: A Product is any offered good or service. Also called item, merchandise, offering. Examples: a pair of shoes, a concert ticket, a car rental service, an episode of a TV show.

candidates.label: SomeProducts
candidates.comment: A placeholder representing multiple similar products of the same kind, used when specific individual products are not distinguished. Also called product group, product category, generic products, similar items. Examples: 'a batch of apples', 'several identical t-shirts', 'a collection of standard screws'.

candidates.label: IndividualProduct
candidates.comment: An IndividualProduct is a single, identifiable instance of a product. Also called specific product unit, unique item, serialized product. Examples: a laptop with a specific serial number, a particular copy of a book, a unique piece of art. Distinct from ProductModel, which describes a class of products, and ProductGroup, which is a collection of products.

candidates.label: Drug
candidates.comment: A Drug is a Product that is a chemical or biological substance used as a medical therapy, having a physiological effect on an organism. Also called medicine, pharmaceutical, medication. Examples: Aspirin, Insulin, Penicillin, Ibuprofen.

candidates.label: Vehicle
candidates.comment: A device designed or used for transporting people or cargo across various environments. Also called conveyance, transport, automobile. Examples: a car, a bicycle, an airplane, a boat, a truck.

types.embedding_query_text: FacilityType: A classification for a type of building or infrastructure designed for a specific purpose. Also called BuildingType, InfrastructureType, VenueType. Examples: data centers.

chosen_type.label: BuildingType
chosen_type.definition: A classification of structures based on their design, purpose, or construction.
chosen_type.justification: None of the candidates represent a general facility type. 'Place' is a suitable parent for a type of location or structure.

candidates.label: USNonprofitType
candidates.comment: An enumeration of specific non-profit organization types recognized within the United States. Also called US charity type, American non-profit category, US voluntary sector classification. Examples: a 501(c)(3) organization, a public charity, a private foundation.

candidates.label: CivicStructure
candidates.comment: A public structure or building intended for public use or government functions. Also called public building, municipal structure, community facility. Examples: A library, a concert hall, a town hall, a park.

candidates.label: NonprofitType
candidates.comment: NonprofitType is an enumeration for various official non-profit organization types. Also called charity type, non-profit classification. Examples: 501(c)(3) (US), Registered Charity (UK), Gemeinnütziger Verein (Germany). Distinct from NLNonprofitType, which is specific to the Netherlands.

candidates.label: UKNonprofitType
candidates.comment: An enumeration of specific non-profit organization types recognized within the United Kingdom. Also called UK charity type, British non-profit category, UK voluntary sector classification. Examples: a registered charity, a community interest company (CIC), a benevolent society.

candidates.label: StadiumOrArena
candidates.comment: A large civic structure designed for sporting events, concerts, or other large-scale public gatherings. Also called stadium, arena, coliseum, sports complex. Examples: Wembley Stadium, Madison Square Garden, the Roman Colosseum.

types.embedding_query_text: ProductPrice: The cost at which a product is sold or offered for sale. Also called GoodsPrice, ItemCost, MerchandisePrice. Examples: Semiconductor and other electronic component manufacturing prices.

chosen_type.label: ProductPrice
chosen_type.definition: The cost at which a product is sold or offered for sale.
chosen_type.justification: No direct schema.org class for 'ProductPrice' was a candidate. 'PriceSpecification' is the closest parent for a specific price.

mentions: Semiconductor and other electronic component manufacturing prices

candidates.label: Product
candidates.comment: A Product is any offered good or service. Also called item, merchandise, offering. Examples: a pair of shoes, a concert ticket, a car rental service, an episode of a TV show.

candidates.label: SomeProducts
candidates.comment: A placeholder representing multiple similar products of the same kind, used when specific individual products are not distinguished. Also called product group, product category, generic products, similar items. Examples: 'a batch of apples', 'several identical t-shirts', 'a collection of standard screws'.

candidates.label: DrugCost
candidates.comment: A DrugCost is a MedicalEntity representing the cost per unit of a medical drug, typically referring to wholesale or average retail cost, not an offer price. Also called medication price, pharmaceutical expense, drug expenditure. Examples: Average retail cost of a prescription, wholesale price of a vaccine, maximum reimbursable cost for a generic drug.

candidates.label: CompoundPriceSpecification
candidates.comment: A price specification that combines multiple prices applicable for different dimensions of consumption. Also called bundled price, multi-component price, composite pricing. Examples: A utility bill with separate charges for electricity and water, a rental agreement with base rent and a "final cleaning" fee, a software license with per-user and per-feature costs. Distinct from PriceSpecification, which is a general description of a price.

candidates.label: SaleEvent
candidates.comment: An event where goods or services are offered for sale, often at reduced prices. Also called sales promotion, discount event, clearance sale, special offer. Examples: a Black Friday sale, an annual warehouse clearance, a seasonal clothing sale, a car dealership's sales event.

types.embedding_query_text: MetricChange: A qualitative description of a change in a measured value, indicating no alteration. Also called NoChange, Constant, Stable. Examples: unchanged.

chosen_type.label: QualitativeValue
chosen_type.justification: 'QualitativeValue' is the best fit for a non-numeric description of a state or change, such as 'unchanged'.

candidates.label: QualitativeValue
candidates.comment: A QualitativeValue is an Enumeration representing a predefined, non-numeric value for a product characteristic. Also called categorical value, descriptive value. Examples: garment size 'S', power cord plug type 'US', color 'red', material 'cotton'. Distinct from QuantitativeValue, which represents a numerical point or interval.

candidates.label: QuantitativeValue
candidates.comment: A QuantitativeValue is a StructuredValue representing a point value or interval for product characteristics or other purposes. Also called numerical value, measurable value. Examples: a product's weight of '5 kg', a temperature range of '20-25°C', a height of '1.8 meters', a price of '$99.99'. Distinct from QualitativeValue, which represents a predefined, non-numeric value.

candidates.label: ExchangeRateSpecification
candidates.comment: An ExchangeRateSpecification is a StructuredValue representing details about an exchange rate. Also called currency exchange rate, foreign exchange rate. Examples: The exchange rate between USD and EUR, a specific conversion rate for a financial transaction, details including fees and validity period.

candidates.label: InstantaneousEvent
candidates.comment: An InstantaneousEvent is a structured value representing an event with no duration, such as a single point in time. Also called momentary event, point event, discrete occurrence. Examples: a computer log entry, a timestamp, a single click on a webpage. Distinct from Event, which typically has a duration.

candidates.label: StatisticalVariable
candidates.comment: A measurable statistical metric that can be observed at a place and time, defined by a population type and specific constraints. Also called statistical metric, data point, observable quantity, measurement variable. Examples: median height of female persons, average temperature in a city, count of news articles published daily. Distinct from StatisticalPopulation, which is the group being measured, not the measurement itself.

types.embedding_query_text: EconomicPressure Examples: localized pressures.

chosen_type.label: EconomicPressure
chosen_type.definition: Forces or conditions that exert strain or influence on an economy or economic agents.
chosen_type.justification: None of the candidates represent the abstract concept of economic pressure. 'Intangible' is a suitable parent for such a concept.

candidates.label: ShippingConditions
candidates.comment: A structured value describing constraints and information about how a product can be shipped, potentially applying to specific product attributes. Also called shipping rules, delivery terms, freight conditions, shipping policy. Examples: free shipping for orders over $50, express shipping for lightweight items, international shipping restrictions.

candidates.label: ExchangeRateSpecification
candidates.comment: An ExchangeRateSpecification is a StructuredValue representing details about an exchange rate. Also called currency exchange rate, foreign exchange rate. Examples: The exchange rate between USD and EUR, a specific conversion rate for a financial transaction, details including fees and validity period.

candidates.label: LocationFeatureSpecification
candidates.comment: A structured value that specifies a feature of an accommodation, represented as a property-value pair. Also called accommodation feature, amenity detail, property value specification. Examples: "hasWifi: true", "numberOfBedrooms: 3", "petsAllowed: false", "poolType: outdoor".

candidates.label: ShippingRateSettings
candidates.comment: A structured value representing reusable shipping rate information, often linked to an offer via a shipping settings link. Also called shipping cost rules, freight pricing, delivery charges configuration. Examples: a flat rate shipping setting for standard delivery, a weight-based shipping rate table, a zone-based shipping cost.

candidates.label: SelfStorage
candidates.comment: A local business providing rental units for individuals and businesses to store their belongings. Also called storage facility, mini-storage, public storage. Examples: 'U-Haul Self-Storage', 'Extra Space Storage', 'Local Storage Units'.
